title: Cloud Accounting Software: Selection, Controls, and Migration
description: A practical checklist for comparing cloud accounting tools by bookkeeping workflow, reconciliation, access controls, integrations, migration, and cost.
author: PilotStack Team

sections.title: Map the work before comparing tools
sections.body: List the people who create invoices, record bills, approve expenses, reconcile transactions, and prepare reports. Write down the current workflow, the systems involved, recurring delays, and the reports the business needs. Record the number of users, entities, currencies, bank accounts, and approximate transaction volume. Use these facts to create must-have requirements before reviewing product demos.

sections.title: Test core bookkeeping tasks
sections.body: Use a trial or demonstration to test the tasks your team performs most often: invoicing, bills, recurring entries, bank feeds, reconciliation, corrections, and period-end reporting. Check whether the system makes duplicate transactions and unresolved differences easy to find. Confirm support for the countries, currencies, and reporting formats relevant to the business using the vendor's current documentation.

sections.title: Review access and audit history
sections.body: Check whether users can be assigned roles that match their responsibilities. Test approval steps, history of edits, locked periods, attachments, and export permissions. Ask how the system records corrections and administrator activity. Where one person should not both prepare and approve a transaction, verify that the workflow can enforce this separation rather than relying on a written policy alone.

sections.title: Check integrations and migration
sections.body: List the connections needed for banking, payments, payroll, inventory, expenses, and the accountant's workflow. Confirm whether each connection is included, separately priced, or maintained by another provider. Before switching, agree which records and historical detail need to move, clean duplicate contacts, and run a trial import. Compare opening balances and key reports with the old system and resolve differences before the cutover date.

sections.title: Compare total cost and support
sections.body: Compare the full plan needed for your user count, reporting, integrations, and support—not just the lowest advertised price. Include setup, migration, training, extra modules, and time spent maintaining connections. Ask about data export, retention, support response times, and how to close the account. Verify current plan details directly with vendors because prices, limits, and package names can change.

sections.title: Run a limited pilot
sections.body: Pilot the tool with a small but representative set of transactions and include both the person doing the work and the person reviewing it. Define pass criteria in advance: accurate reconciliation, usable reports, clear edit history, reliable exports, and a manageable close process. Keep the previous system available until the new workflow has been checked and signed off by the people responsible for the records.

faqs.question: Can software replace professional accounting review?
faqs.answer: Software can streamline routine recording and reporting, but complex decisions and formal reporting may still require a qualified professional who understands the business and its obligations.

faqs.question: What should be checked before switching systems?
faqs.answer: Confirm the records to migrate, compare opening balances and key reports, test exports, and keep an accessible archive of the old system.

faqs.question: How should I compare pricing?
faqs.answer: Compare the same users, transaction volume, modules, integrations, and support needs. Include setup and migration costs and confirm current limits with the vendor.
